title: Server-Side Discovery
description: Learn how server-side discovery works and when to use it.

data.text: Server-side discovery centralizes load balancing in a dedicated component like a load balancer or proxy. AWS, Azure, and Kubernetes all use this pattern because it simplifies clients and provides a single point for traffic management.

In server-side discovery, clients send requests to a load balancer or proxy. The load balancer queries the service registry, selects an instance, and forwards the request. Clients remain simple and do not need discovery logic.

data.title: Server-Side Discovery Flow
items: Client sends request to load balancer or proxy
Load balancer selects an instance using a load-balancing algorithm
Load balancer forwards the request to the selected instance
Instance responds to the load balancer, which returns the response to the client

data.title: Popular Tools
items: AWS Elastic Load Balancer (ELB): Cloud load balancer with auto-discovery
NGINX: Open-source load balancer with dynamic upstream
Kubernetes Services: Built-in load balancing via kube-proxy

data.title: Kubernetes Service Discovery
data.text: Kubernetes Services provide built-in server-side discovery. The kube-proxy component watches for Pod changes and updates iptables or IPVS rules to route traffic to healthy instances.

data.title: Example: NGINX with Consul Template

items.question: Is server-side discovery simpler than client-side?
items.answer: Yes, for clients. The load balancer handles all discovery and load-balancing logic. However, you need to manage and scale the load balancer itself.

items.question: Does the load balancer become a bottleneck?
items.answer: A properly sized load balancer can handle millions of requests per second. Cloud providers like AWS offer auto-scaling load balancers.

items.question: What about the extra network hop?
items.answer: In cloud environments, the extra hop is usually negligible compared to the benefits of centralized traffic management and simplified clients.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Clients remain simple and do not need discovery logic
Common in Kubernetes and cloud environments
Load balancer must be highly available
data.takeaway: Server-side discovery is the default choice in containerized and cloud-native environments.
